g.text: CHAPTER I • THE TANDOOR & SIGRI
Folio 01
MENUQR ROYAL ARCHIVES • ESTD 1924
ROYAL AWADHI GRILLS
THE ART OF GALOUTI & TANDOOR
Galouti Kebab Nawabi
Young pasture mutton pounded 4 times into an ethereal silk purée, infused with 160 secret
botanical herbs, and smoked over burning cloves and aged cow ghee. Melts on the tongue.
Accompaniment: Ulte Tawe Ka Saffron Paratha & Mint Onion Relish
Bhatti Murgh Angara
Boneless chicken thigh steeped 24 hours in pungent yellow mustard oil, Mathania chillies,
and crushed stone black cardamom, then roasted over live charcoal until crisped.
Garnished with pickled charred shallots and fresh pomegranate pearls
Royal Paneer Pasanda
Twin fillets of fresh Malai Paneer stuffed with golden sultanas, pistachios and khoya,
pan-seared in cow ghee, enveloped in a satin brown onion and cashew velouté.
THE ROYAL KEBAB PROCLAMATION
DECREE OF THE ROYAL AWADHI KEBABS • ESTD 1784
"The kebabs of Awadh have no need for teeth;"
"Crafted with such grace that they dissolve upon the gentlest touch."
"When the aging Nawab of Awadh lost his teeth to the passage of time,
his royal Khansamas spent seven seasons blending dried rose petals,
vetiver roots, and raw papaya into meat so gentle, it dissolved
on the tongue like sweet morning dew on a jasmine bud."
— Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula • Court of Awadh, Lucknow (1784)
ROYAL KEBAB RECIPE NO. 14 • ARCHIVES OF AWADH
CHAPTER I • THE TANDOOR & SIGRI
Folio 02
MENUQR ROYAL ARCHIVES • ESTD 1924
ROYAL VEGETARIAN SELECTIONS
DELICACIES OF THE COAL EMBER
Awadhi Dahi Ke Kebab
Silk hung curd folded with roasted gram flour, finely minced mint, green cardamom and black pepper,
crisped golden in cow ghee to yield a molten cream core that dissolves upon touch.
Tandoori Malai Broccoli
Tender broccoli crowns steeped in cardamom cream, processed cheddar, roasted cashew cream,
and white pepper, char-grilled over acacia wood coals for subtle smokiness.
Kakori Kebab Royale
Finest minced kid mutton infused with wild khus (vetiver), mace, dried rose petals,
and rendered kidney fat, grilled gently on sword skewers over low coals.
THE LAW OF THE COAL
THE ARTISANAL PRINCIPLE OF CLAY & SMOKE
"Slow embers of acacia charcoal and generations of dedication;"
"Therein lies the true, exquisite delicacy of Awadhi cooking."
"No modern gas flame can replicate what four hours of slow
acacia charcoal embers whisper into marinated cream, meat, and curd.
The heat must never hurry; it must breathe with quiet nobility,
imparting the fragrance of sacred woods into every pore."
— Khansama Haji Mohammad Ismail • Chief Pitmaster (Estd 1924)
TEMPERED IN CLAY OVEN AT 320°C • 100% HARDWOOD COALS
